lower-middle.notes: Sleeve boundaries measured at y700, y1500 and y2400 in the EXIF-oriented 4032x3024 original. Endpoints conservatively inset to y650..2600 and extrapolated only 50px above /200px below the measured cuts. Each side is independently traced; wide Mahler box and leaning Rampal/Laskine spine use measured seams. Thin, heavily worn or overlapping sleeve edges are estimates bounded by adjacent visible sleeves; all catalog IDs are retained, with the three Bowie titles mapped to photographed physical order. Shapes deliberately avoid exposed interior wall and the white outer frame. The last sleeves end far left of the opening right boundary; slot67 specifically follows the cream Japanese Melodies sleeve. Central strips are represented, excluding ragged folded tips and some sleeve ends.
lower-middle.sourceOrientation: EXIF orientation3 applied; browser displayed pixels

upper-middle.notes: Two physical compartments. Individually measured source x seam anchors at y700 and y2400, with side-edge interpolation at y1500. Per-sleeve cap and foot heights measured from full-resolution endpoint crops now extend each outline to its photographed sleeve corners, approximately2-4px inside the sleeve. Existing side seam slopes are retained; left/right endpoint heights vary independently. The front divider and exposed white frame remain excluded. Rounded wear and tiny folded corner peaks are approximated by straight cap/foot edges. Nitty Gritty Dirt Band three-record box, Pink Floyd double sleeve and Elton John sleeve retain their measured larger widths. Unreadable, heavily worn or partly overlapping seams use bounded estimates; all68 original catalog IDs are retained. The rightmost cream sleeve is inset from the angled exposed white interior wall.
upper-middle.sourceOrientation: EXIF orientation3 applied; browser displayed pixels

method: Manual sleeve-edge anchor measurements on analysis crops from the original EXIF-oriented photos. Piecewise-linear sides, conservative2px inset. These are interactive central-face masks, not pixel-perfect sleeve segmentation. No original photo pixels are changed.
